explanation: A judge in Israel who led the nation for 23 years and helped maintain peace and justice.
Another judge in Israel who ruled for 22 years and sought to promote justice and stability in the land.
An ancient Semitic people group who were enemies of Israel and often came into conflict with them.
Another hostile people group against Israel, known for their military strength and conflicts with the Israelites.
A Canaanite god whom the Israelites began to worship, leading them away from their own God.
An area east of the Jordan River inhabited by the Israelites that played an important role in the stories in the book of Judges.
Sorrow and regret over past actions, especially regarding turning away from God and worshipping other gods.
A judge and warrior chosen to lead Israel in battle against the Ammonites, who made a vow to God to sacrifice the first person he met upon returning home after victory.
A commitment or agreement between two parties, in this case between Jephthah and God, involving mutual understanding and expectation of keeping the promise.
